text: It starts with old red blood cells.
They live up to a hundred and twenty days.
Then macrophages in your spleen, liver and bone marrow break them down.
Heme loses its iron and becomes green biliverdin, then yellow bilirubin.
Bilirubin rides your blood to the liver.
Your liver puts it into bile, about half a liter to a liter a day.
Your gallbladder stores that bile and concentrates it.
When you eat, bile flows into the duodenum to help break up fats.
In your large intestine, bacteria turn bilirubin into urobilinogen, then stercobilin.
Stercobilin is the brown in your poop.
And the yellow in your urine? Urobilins, cleared by your kidneys.
